questions.q: Integrating factor of the differential equation $(1-x^2)\dfrac{dy}{dx}-xy=1$ is
questions.explanation: Writing as $\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{x}{1-x^2}y=\dfrac{1}{1-x^2}$, I.F. $=e^{\int -\frac{x}{1-x^2}dx}=e^{\frac12\ln(1-x^2)}=\sqrt{1-x^2}$.

questions.q: $\int xf(x)dx+\dfrac{f(x)}{2}=0$, then $f(x)$ is equal to
questions.explanation: Differentiating the given relation, $xf(x)+\tfrac12f'(x)=0\Rightarrow \dfrac{f'(x)}{f(x)}=-2x\Rightarrow \ln f(x)=-x^2+C\Rightarrow f(x)=Ce^{-x^2}$.

questions.q: Sum of the squares of the order and degree (if defined) of a differential equation $2y'+(y'')^2=\sqrt{y''-3}$ is
questions.explanation: The order is 2 (from $y''$). Squaring to remove the radical makes $(y'')^4$ the highest power, so the degree is 4. Sum of squares $=2^2+4^2=4+16=20$.

questions.q: General solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y\tan x=\sec x$ is
questions.explanation: Integrating factor is sec x; multiplying and integrating gives y sec x = tan x + c.

questions.q: If 'a' and 'b' are the order and degree respectively of the differentiable equation $\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^3+x^4=0$, then a - b =
questions.explanation: The order is 2 (highest derivative) and the degree is 2 (power of highest derivative term), so a - b = 0.

questions.q: The solution of $e^{\frac{dy}{dx}}=x+1, y(0)=3$ is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\log(x+1) \Rightarrow y=(x+1)\log(x+1)-(x+1)+C$. Using $y(0)=3$ gives $C=4$, which rearranges to $y+x-3=(x+1)\log(x+1)$.

questions.q: The family of curves whose x and y intercepts of a tangent at any point are respectively double the x and y coordinates of that point is
questions.explanation: If the tangent at $(x_1,y_1)$ has intercepts $2x_1,2y_1$, its equation gives the differential equation $x\,dy+y\,dx=0$ whose solution is $xy=C$.

questions.q: If a curve passes through the point $(1, 1)$ and at any point $(x, y)$ on the curve, the product of the slope of its tangent and x co-ordinate of the point is equal to the y co-ordinate of the point, then the curve also passes through the point
questions.explanation: $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}=y \Rightarrow y=kx$; through $(1,1)$, $k=1$ so $y=x$, which passes through $(2,2)$.

questions.q: The degree of the differential equation $1 + \left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2 + \left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^2 = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}+1}$ is
questions.explanation: Cubing both sides to remove the cube root gives a polynomial equation in which the highest-order derivative $d^2y/dx^2$ appears with power 6, so the degree is 6.

questions.q: The sum of the degree and order of the differential equation $(1+y_1^2)^{2/3} = y_2$ is
questions.explanation: Cubing both sides gives $(1+y_1^2)^2=y_2^3$, a polynomial equation of degree 3 in the highest derivative $y_2$ (order 2). Sum = 2+3 = 5.

questions.q: If $\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{y}{x} = x^2$, then 2y(2) - y(1) =
questions.explanation: IF = x, giving $xy=\frac{x^4}{4}+C$, so $y=\frac{x^3}{4}+\frac{C}{x}$. Then $2y(2)-y(1)=2\left(2+\frac C2\right)-\left(\frac14+C\right)=4-\frac14=\frac{15}{4}$ (C cancels).

questions.q: The solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx} = (x+y)^2$ is
questions.explanation: Put $v=x+y$: $\frac{dv}{dx}=1+v^2$, so $\tan^{-1}v = x+c$, i.e. $\tan^{-1}(x+y)=x+c$.

questions.q: If y(x) be the solution of differential equation $x\log x\dfrac{dy}{dx} + y = 2x\log x$, y(e) is equal to
questions.explanation: The general solution is $y\ln x = 2x\ln x - 2x + C$. Requiring y to stay finite (regular) as $x\to1$ (where $\ln x\to0$) forces $C=2$, giving $y(e)=2e-2e+2=2$. The question's answer is genuinely ambiguous without this extra regularity condition (no initial value is explicitly given), which is likely why KEA awarded a grace mark. (as per KEA key)

questions.q: Solution of Differential Equation xdy $-$ ydx = 0 represents
options: Parabola whose vertex is at origin
A circle whose centre is origin
questions.explanation: Separating variables, dy/y = dx/x, giving y = kx, a straight line through the origin.

questions.q: The number of solutions of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\dfrac{y+1}{x-1}$ when y(1) = 2 is
questions.explanation: The initial point x=1 is a singular point of the equation (denominator vanishes there); KEA's key accepts both 'one' and 'infinite' as correct.

questions.q: The order of the differential equation obtained by eliminating arbitrary constants in the family of curves $c_1y=(c_2+c_3)e^{x+c_4}$ is
questions.explanation: $(c_2+c_3)e^{c_4}$ combines into a single constant, so $y=Ke^x$ has only one independent arbitrary constant, giving order 1.

questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation $x^2dy-2xy\,dx=x^4\cos x\,dx$ is
questions.explanation: Dividing by $x^2$ gives a linear ODE with integrating factor $x^{-2}$; solving yields $y=x^2\sin x+cx^2$.

questions.q: The curve passing through the point $(1, 2)$ given that the slope of the tangent at any point $(x, y)$ is $\dfrac{2x}{y}$ represents
questions.explanation: Solving $y\,dy=2x\,dx$ gives $y^2-2x^2=2$ after using $(1,2)$, which is a hyperbola.

questions.q: The order of the differential equation $y = C_1e^{C_2+x} + C_3e^{C_4+x}$ is
questions.explanation: $y=(C_1e^{C_2}+C_3e^{C_4})e^x=Ke^x$ has only one essential arbitrary constant, so the order is 1.

questions.q: The integrating factor of the differential equation $(2x+3y^2)\,dy = y\,dx\ (y>0)$ is
questions.explanation: Writing as $\dfrac{dx}{dy}-\dfrac{2}{y}x=3y$ (linear in $x$), the integrating factor is $e^{\int -2/y\,dy}=y^{-2}$.

questions.q: The equation of the curve passing through the point (1, 1) such that the slope of the tangent at any point $(x,y)$ is equal to the product of its co-ordinates is
questions.explanation: $\dfrac{dy}{y}=x\,dx\Rightarrow \ln y=\dfrac{x^2}{2}+C$; using $(1,1)$ gives $C=-\dfrac12$, i.e. $2\log y=x^2-1$.

questions.q: The degree and the order of the differential equation $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}=\sqrt[3]{1+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2}$ respectively are
questions.explanation: Cubing gives $\left(\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}\right)^3=1+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2$; degree = 3, order = 2.

questions.q: The solution of the differential equation $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}-y=3$ represents a family of
questions.explanation: Solving the linear ODE gives $y=Cx-3$, a family of straight lines.

questions.q: The integrating factor of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=\dfrac{1+y}{x}$ is
questions.explanation: Rewriting as $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y\left(1-\dfrac1x\right)=\dfrac1x$, the integrating factor is $e^{x-\ln x}=\dfrac{e^x}{x}$.

questions.q: The degree of the differential equation $\left[1+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2\right]^2=\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ is
questions.explanation: The highest order derivative $\dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$ occurs to the power 1, so the degree is 1.

questions.q: General solution of differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+y=1\ (y\ne1)$ is
questions.explanation: Separating variables, $\dfrac{dy}{1-y}=dx$; integrating gives $-\log|1-y|=x+C$, i.e. $\log\left|\dfrac{1}{1-y}\right|=x+C$.

questions.q: The integrating factor of the differential equation $x\cdot\dfrac{dy}{dx}+2y=x^2$ is $(x\ne0)$
questions.explanation: Writing as $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac2xy=x$, the integrating factor is $e^{\int(2/x)dx}=e^{2\log x}=x^2$.

questions.q: The solution for the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{y} + \dfrac{dx}{x} = 0$ is
questions.explanation: Integrating, $\ln y+\ln x=c_1 \Rightarrow \ln(xy)=c_1 \Rightarrow xy=c$.

questions.q: The order and degree of the differential equation $\left[1+\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)^2+\sin\left(\dfrac{dy}{dx}\right)\right]^{3/4} = \dfrac{d^2y}{dx^2}$
questions.explanation: The highest derivative is $d^2y/dx^2$, so order is 2; since the equation contains $\sin(dy/dx)$, a transcendental function of a derivative, the degree is not defined.

questions.q: Integrating factor of $x\dfrac{dy}{dx} - y = x^4 - 3x$ is
questions.explanation: Dividing by x gives $\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{y}{x}=x^3-3$, a linear equation with $P=-1/x$; IF $=e^{\int -1/x\,dx}=e^{-\ln x}=1/x$.

questions.q: The order of differential equation of all circles of given radius 'a' is ____
questions.explanation: The family $(x-h)^2+(y-k)^2=a^2$ has two arbitrary constants $h,k$, so the order of its differential equation is 2.

questions.q: The solution of differential equation $x\dfrac{dy}{dx}+2y=x^2$ is ____
questions.explanation: This is linear with I.F. $x^2$: $yx^2=\int x^3\,dx=\dfrac{x^4}{4}+C_1$, giving $y=\dfrac{x^4+4C_1}{4x^2}$, matching option (4).

questions.q: The order and degree of the differential equation y = x $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{2}{\dfrac{dy}{dx}}$ is
questions.explanation: Writing $p=dy/dx$ and clearing the fraction gives $xp^2-yp+2=0$, a first order equation of degree 2.

questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation $\dfrac{dy}{dx}+\dfrac{y}{x}=3x$ is
questions.explanation: Integrating factor is x. $(xy)'=3x^2 \Rightarrow xy=x^3+C \Rightarrow y=x^2+C/x$; since C is an arbitrary constant, option (2) with $-C/x$ is equivalent.

questions.q: If $f(x)=f'(x)+f''(x)+f'''(x)+\ldots$ and $f(0)=1$, then $f(x)=$
questions.explanation: Differentiating shows $f'(x)=f(x)-f'(x)$, so $2f'=f$, giving $f(x)=e^{x/2}$ since $f(0)=1$.

questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation $\sqrt{1-x^2y^2}\cdot dx=y\cdot dx+x\cdot dy$ is
questions.explanation: Since $y\,dx+x\,dy=d(xy)$, the equation becomes $\sqrt{1-u^2}\,dx=du$ with $u=xy$, integrating to $u=\sin(x+c)$, i.e. $\sin(x+c)=xy$.

questions.q: If 'm' and 'n' are the order and degree of the differential equation $(y'')^5+4\cdot\dfrac{(y'')^3}{y'''}+y'''=\sin x$, then
questions.explanation: Clearing the fraction by multiplying through by $y'''$ gives $(y'')^5y'''+4(y'')^3+(y''')^2=y'''\sin x$, a polynomial equation of order 3 (highest derivative $y'''$) and degree 2.

questions.q: Solution of $e^{\frac{dy}{dx}} = x$ when $x = 1$ and $y = 0$ is
questions.explanation: $dy/dx=\log x$, so $y=x\log x-x+C$. Using $x=1,y=0$ gives $C=1$, so $y=x(\log x-1)+1$.

questions.q: If $m$ and $n$ are degree and order of $\left(1+y_1^2\right)^{2/3}=y_2$, then the value of $\dfrac{m+n}{m-n}$ is ............
questions.explanation: Cubing both sides gives $(1+y_1^2)^2=y_2^3$, a polynomial equation with order $n=2$ (highest derivative $y_2$) and degree $m=3$. So $\dfrac{m+n}{m-n}=\dfrac{5}{1}=5$.

questions.q: The general solution of $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=1-x^2-y^2+x^2y^2$ is ............
questions.explanation: The right side factors as $(1-x^2)(1-y^2)$. Taking this to mean $\dfrac{dy}{dx}=\sqrt{(1-x^2)(1-y^2)}$ (the intended equation, since the printed form without a square root does not lead to any listed answer), separating variables gives $\sin^{-1}y=\dfrac x2\sqrt{1-x^2}+\dfrac12\sin^{-1}x+C$, i.e. $2\sin^{-1}y=x\sqrt{1-x^2}+\sin^{-1}x+c$. KEA awarded a grace mark for this question.

questions.q: The order and degree of the differential equation $y=\dfrac{dp}{dx}x+\sqrt{a^2p^2+b^2}$ where $p=\dfrac{dy}{dx}$ (here $a$ and $b$ are arbitrary constants) respectively are
questions.explanation: $dp/dx=d^2y/dx^2$, so the order is 2; isolating and squaring the radical, $(y-xp')^2=a^2p^2+b^2$, makes the highest derivative appear squared, so the degree is also 2.

questions.q: The general solution of the differential equation $2x\dfrac{dy}{dx}-y=3$ is a family of
questions.explanation: Solving the linear equation gives $y=C\sqrt x-3$, i.e. $(y+3)^2=C^2x$, which represents a family of parabolas.

questions.q: The differential equation of the family of circles passing through the origin and having their centres on the x-axis is
questions.explanation: Such circles are $x^2+y^2-2ax=0$; differentiating gives $a=x+y y'$, and substituting back into $a=(x^2+y^2)/2x$ gives $y^2=x^2+2xy\,dy/dx$.

questions.q: A population grows at the rate of 10% of the population per year. How long does it take for the population to double?
questions.explanation: $dP/dt=0.1P \Rightarrow P=P_0e^{0.1t}$; doubling needs $e^{0.1t}=2 \Rightarrow t = 10\ln2$.
